claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys below about 1200 K.
Diffuse antiphase boundaries produced by SRO act as strong phonon-scattering centers.
At temperatures above about 1800 K, thermal entropy disrupts SRO in MoNbTaW.
Thermal disruption of SRO reduces the phonon-scattering cross-section and increases the phonon mean free path.
At high temperature, the lattice thermal conductivity of the SRO alloy converges toward that of the random solid solution.
The investigated initial material is bcc MoNbTaW in a random-solid-solution or negligible-SRO state.
Equilibration at 800 K induces chemical SRO in MoNbTaW.
Breaking local chemical order during lattice deformation or dislocation glide creates diffuse antiphase boundaries.
Thermal excitation alone creates diffuse antiphase boundaries by breaking up local order.
Using low applied shear stress minimizes dislocation-mediated thermal-transport contributions and isolates lattice phonon effects.
Diffuse antiphase boundaries create a spatially fluctuating potential landscape for phonons.
SRO or its diffuse antiphase boundaries produce periodic or semiperiodic modulation of atomic mass and bonding stiffness.
The SRO-induced modulation resonantly scatters mid- to high-frequency phonons and reduces their mean free path.
The SRO sample will exhibit more than a 15% reduction in lattice thermal conductivity relative to the RSS sample at 300 K.
The SRO–RSS lattice-thermal-conductivity difference will become negligible at 2000 K.
The SRO strengthening effect on screw-dislocation motion becomes negligible at 2000 K.
Similar W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf systems have an order-disorder transition temperature of approximately 1120 K.
The proposed suppression applies when phonon wavelengths are comparable to the SRO correlation length.
Long-range precipitation would introduce interface or grain-boundary scattering distinct from diffuse-antiphase-boundary scattering.
The cited evidence contains simulations of dislocation mechanics but no direct phonon-transport or thermal-conductivity measurements or simulations.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis assigns the low-temperature suppression regime to temperatures below 1200 K, while the boundary limits applicability to an approximate order-disorder transition below 1120 K, leaving the 1120–1200 K interval inconsistent.

The mediator is said to arise through breakup of SRO during deformation, but the conditions minimize deformation/dislocation activity and the experiment does not specify a deformation step that would generate the proposed DAPBs.
